question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y + 6 x^{2} y=- 3 x y^{2}\,.
$$

Assume $y\ne 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)\,,
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y + 6 x^{2} y=- 3 x y^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y + 6 x^{2} y + 3 x y^{2}=0 \\ y (\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + 6 x^{2} + 3 x y)=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + 6 x^{2} + 3 x y=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(3 x)}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{- 6 x^{2}}_{Q(x)} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + 3 x y=- 6 x^{2}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=3 x$ and $Q(x)=- 6 x^{2}.$

Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
3 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + 4 \cos{(x )}=- 8 y \sin{(x )} - 3\,.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{gathered}3 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + 4 \cos{(x )}=- 8 y \sin{(x )} - 3 \\ 3 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + 8 y \sin{(x )}=- 4 \cos{(x )} - 3 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(\frac{8 \sin{(x )}}{3})}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{- \frac{4 \cos{(x )}}{3} - 1}_{Q(x)}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=\frac{8 \sin{(x )}}{3}$ and $Q(x)=- \frac{4 \cos{(x )}}{3} - 1.$

A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} \cos{(6 x )} + 6 y \sin{(6 x )} + 4 \sin{(12 x )}=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} \cos{(6 x )} + 6 y \sin{(6 x )}=- 4 \sin{(12 x )} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + \frac{6 y \sin{(6 x )}}{\cos{(6 x )}}=- \frac{4 \sin{(12 x )}}{\cos{(6 x )}} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + 6 y \tan{(6 x )}=\frac{- 8 \sin{(6 x )}\cos{(6 x )}}{\cos{(6 x )}} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(6 \tan{(6 x )})}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{- 8 \sin{(6 x )}}_{Q(x)}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=6 \tan{(6 x )}$ and $Q(x)=- 8 \sin{(6 x )}.$

$$
\left(\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{- 7 x - 3 y}{x}\,.
$$

Assume $x\ne 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)\,,
$$

where $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ do not depend on $y.$

We have

$$
\begin{gathered}\left(\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{- 7 x - 3 y}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=x^{2}\left(\frac{- 7 x - 3 y}{x}\right) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=x (- 7 x - 3 y) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=- 7 x^{2} - 3 x y \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(3 x)}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{- 7 x^{2}}_{Q(x)} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + 3 x y=- 7 x^{2}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=3 x$ and $Q(x)=- 7 x^{2}.$
